description: NaSn₂Cl₅ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pnnm space group. Na¹⁺ is bonded to six Cl¹⁻ atoms to form NaCl₆ octahedra that share corners with four equivalent SnCl₅ square pyramids and edges with two equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Na-Cl bond distances ranging from 2.80-2.86 Å. There are two inequivalent Sn²⁺ sites. In the first Sn²⁺ site, Sn²⁺ is bonded to five Cl¹⁻ atoms to form distorted SnCl₅ square pyramids that share corners with four equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra and  an edgeedge with one SnCl₅ square pyramid. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 54-80°. There are a spread of Sn-Cl bond distances ranging from 2.55-3.06 Å. In the second Sn²⁺ site, Sn²⁺ is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to three Cl¹⁻ atoms. There is one shorter (2.58 Å) and two longer (2.59 Å) Sn-Cl bond lengths. There are four inequivalent Cl¹⁻ sites. In the first Cl¹⁻ site, Cl¹⁻ is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to two equivalent Na¹⁺ and one Sn²⁺ atom. In the second Cl¹⁻ site, Cl¹⁻ is bonded in a water-like geometry to two equivalent Sn²⁺ atoms. In the third Cl¹⁻ site, Cl¹⁻ is bonded in a distorted trigonal non-coplanar geometry to one Na¹⁺ and two Sn²⁺ atoms. In the fourth Cl¹⁻ site, Cl¹⁻ is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to two equivalent Na¹⁺ and one Sn²⁺ atom.
